team.claim: Alex Bouaziz is co-founder and CEO of Deel (listed on the company's leadership page).
Shuo Wang is co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) of Deel.
In November 2025 Deel appointed former Intuit executive Joe Kauffman as President and Chief Financial Officer, signalling IPO intent; he is listed as President and CFO on the leadership page.
Dan Westgarth is Chief Operating Officer; he is also named as a defendant in Rippling's amended complaint.
Philippe Bouaziz is Executive Chairman & Chief Strategy Officer; Rippling's amended complaint alleges a 'Bouaziz Racketeering Enterprise' directed by CEO Alex Bouaziz and his father.
Other executives: Yaron Lavi (CTO), Harish Sharma (Chief Risk Officer), DeAnn Work (Global Corporate General Counsel), Anthony Rodriguez (Chief Compliance Officer).
Also during 2025, Deel appointed a chief risk officer, chief compliance officer and general counsel — a build-out of the compliance bench.
Ofer Simon is listed by Wikipedia as a 2019 co-founder but does not appear on Deel's current leadership page; no public departure announcement was found in pages opened.

CEO Alex Bouaziz told Fortune that 80% of his leadership team is the same as when the company was at $0 ARR, and that he ignored advice to replace early leadership as the company scaled; workforce grew from 10 to 3,600 workers per the article.
Founders' background: Bouaziz and Wang met while studying at MIT in 2013; Bouaziz studied engineering at the Technion and was 25 when he launched Deel in 2019.

output.company: Deel, Inc. (deel.com) — global payroll, HR and employer-of-record platform, San Francisco, CA

funding.claim: Series A, May 2020: $14 million led by Andreessen Horowitz (Wikipedia; aggregator AccessIPOs lists $18.61M at $63M valuation).

Series B, September 2020: $30 million at ~$230M valuation, led by Spark Capital with Y Combinator, William Hockey, Ryan Petersen, Nat Friedman, John Zimmer and Alexis Ohanian (Dealroom; AccessIPOs table; Wikipedia cites $48M — sources conflict on amount).
Series C, April 2021: $156 million with a16z participation, making Deel a unicorn (aggregators list ~$1.14-1.3B valuation).
Series D, October 2021: $425 million led by Coatue and DST Global at a $5.5 billion valuation.

May 2022: new funding of ~$50 million (with Emerson Collective per Wikipedia) at a $12 billion valuation, up from $5.5 billion in late 2021; at that time CEO Alex Bouaziz disclosed a $100 million ARR rate.
Earlier in 2025 (February): Deel was valued at $12.6 billion after a $300 million secondary purchase by General Catalyst and Abu Dhabi's Mubadala.

Series E, October 2025: $300 million led by new investor Ribbit Capital alongside existing backers Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue, valuing Deel at $17.3 billion; capital earmarked for acquisitions and native payroll in 100+ countries by 2029.

Aggregator (AccessIPOs) round table: Series A 05/20 ($63M val), Series B 08/20 ($230M val), Series C 04/21 ($1.14B), Series D 07/21 ($5.5B), Series D3 05/22 ($12.1B), Series E 10/15/25 ($17.3B, $300M) — labelled aggregator data.
IPO: Deel is still aiming for a 2026 US initial public offering, but it depends on macroeconomic conditions (CEO Alex Bouaziz to Reuters, June 2025).
In February 2025 CEO Alex Bouaziz said Deel was preparing for a potential IPO, 'getting ready to go out, potentially next year or a bit later.'

output.verdict: Deel looks commercially strong: roughly $1B+ run-rate revenue with ~75% YoY growth and ~16% EBITDA margin (company-reported), 35,000-40,000+ customers in 150+ countries, top-tier backers (Ribbit, a16z, Coatue) at a $17.3B valuation, and an aggressive 13-acquisition roll-up. What needs a closer look is everything around the edge of the machine: a reported DOJ criminal probe (Jan 2026) and active Rippling espionage/RICO litigation — with unsealed bank records showing a spy payment routed via the COO's wife and Deel's admitted surveillance of the witness — plus a compliance history (MyForexFunds, a dismissed AML/sanctions suit, 2023 misclassification claims) that questions whether controls kept pace with hypergrowth. Until the DOJ probe and the trade-secret claims resolve, headline financials are un-audited company claims and legal tail risk should be priced into any valuation.

business.claim: Deel, Inc. is an American payroll and HR company incorporated in Delaware that operates remotely with a globally distributed workforce; it provides hiring, payments and workforce management for companies hiring international employees and contractors.

Deel offers employer-of-record, contractor, immigration, HRIS and performance-management services, owns around 250 entities globally, and manages in-house in-country payroll teams in over 130 countries.
Deel's own site markets Deel Payroll, Deel HR, Deel IT, Deel Benefits, Deel Hire, Deel Mobility, Deel Embedded, Deel Services, plus EOR and PEO offerings.
Company claim: Deel serves 35,000+ customers in over 150 countries with 6,500+ team members worldwide in over 100 countries (March 2024).
Reuters describes Deel as San Francisco, California-based; customers use its global payroll platform to manage their international workforce, and it competes with Rippling, Omnipresent and ADP.

Aggregator description: Deel generates revenue through subscription fees for its platform plus additional charges for specialized services such as immigration assistance and compliance monitoring (Dealroom).
Deel was founded in 2019 by Alex Bouaziz (CEO), Shuo Wang (CRO) and Ofer Simon, and launched after entering the Y Combinator accelerator in 2019.
Geographies: Deel operates across 150+ countries (customers) with ~250 owned entities and in-country payroll teams in 130+ countries; Wikipedia lists headcount of 7,500 (2025).

traction.claim: Named customers per Reuters: AI startup ElevenLabs, Nike, Klarna and Shopify, among 35,000+ customers (company statement reported by Reuters).
Company claim: 35,000-plus customers including Reddit, Klarna and Cloudflare (March 2024, Deel blog announcing PaySpace acquisition).
Company-published case studies on deel.com: Revolut, FICO, Puma, Outreach, Zip Co and Directional Pizza.
Growth statement (company claim reported by Reuters): revenue rose 75% for the twelve months ended April 30, 2025.
Deel crossed $1 billion annual revenue run rate in Q1 2025 and earmarked an M&A budget of $200-500 million for 2025 (company statements reported by Reuters).
Company claim (via Reuters citation): the platform processes payments for more than 1.5 million workers in over 150 countries and serves more than 35,000 clients.
Deel acquired African native-payroll company PaySpace in March 2024, its second buyout of 2024, bringing it to ~$500M ARR (company claim).
Deel acquired Safeguard Global's payroll division in March 2025 for an undisclosed amount (reported by Reuters).
Deel recently acquired London-based competitor Omnipresent in a deal worth around $15 million, according to a person familiar with the matter (Reuters).
By the end of 2025 Deel had acquired 13 companies, including Zeitgold, Roots, Paygroup, Legalpad, Capbase, Zavvy, PaySpace, Hofy, Atlantic Money, Assemble and Safeguard Global's payroll division.
Deel acquired Israeli AI cybersecurity firm Clarity in August 2026.
Sponsorships: in December 2025 Arsenal F.C. announced Deel as the club's new HR partner, and in May 2026 Deel became Arsenal's sleeve sponsor.
Recognition: CNBC Disruptor 50 (2024) and top 10 of the Forbes Cloud 100 2025 list (September 2025).
Aggregator data (ARR.club, unverified by primary sources): Deel reached $1.2B ARR Oct 2025, $1.4B in March 2026 with 40K+ customers, and $1.5B by August 2026 (+19% annualized CAGR).

red_flags.claim: Federal criminal exposure: the DOJ reportedly opened a criminal investigation into Deel (WSJ, Jan 23, 2026) over the corporate-spy allegations, elevating a civil dispute into potential criminal liability.

Unsealed bank records show Deel's payment to the confessed spy was routed through an account belonging to the wife of Deel's COO (funds arrived 56 seconds later) — an optics and controls red flag flagged by Rippling's lawyers to Deel's auditors.
Deel admitted in court (Irish Times via TechCrunch) that it instructed 'discreet surveillance' on the manager at the centre of the spy case, after its lawyer initially denied it.

Rippling's amended complaint adds RICO charges and names Deel's CEO, Chairman (Philippe Bouaziz) and COO (Dan Westgarth) as defendants in an alleged 'criminal syndicate'/'Bouaziz Racketeering Enterprise' that targeted at least four competitors.

Compliance history: Deel facilitated $72M+ in payments (40,000+ transactions, 15,664 customers) for MyForexFunds, a prop-trading platform the CFTC accused of running a Ponzi scheme, before freezing the account — a pattern relevant to AML/KYC scrutiny of a payments-heavy business.

Worker-classification exposure: former Deel workers claimed mis-categorization (March 2023) and a California state senator requested a state labor-agency investigation (June 2023); Deel denied the allegations.

Litigation risk persists into 2026: the Rippling case is in discovery with RICO claims cleared to proceed after a February 2026 ruling, while Deel's own Delaware countersuit was voluntarily dismissed — unresolved espionage claims remain live.

Information risk for diligence: all revenue, profitability and ARR figures are company statements (no audited financials or S-1 publicly available); the only post-Oct-2025 ARR data ($1.4B-$1.5B) comes from aggregator ARR.club, unverified.

reputation.claim: Employee reviews (Glassdoor, social/aggregator data): rating 4.3/5 from 2,132 reviews; 83% would recommend to a friend; 88% approve of CEO Alex Bouaziz; 82% positive business outlook; 24 new reviews in the last month.
Glassdoor names Deel a Best Places to Work winner for 2025, citing a supportive remote-first culture, while some reviews flag workload/burnout and communication concerns in a fast-paced environment.
Customer reviews (company-cited): Deel's homepage shows 4.7/5 based on 15,401 G2 reviews — company-published figure.

Critical press sentiment reached practitioner communities: a January 2025 r/sales thread on the money-laundering/Ponzi-scheme lawsuit drew 74 comments and 85 upvotes; a January 2024 r/sales thread asked 'Does anybody know anything about DEEL?' (36 comments) — social sentiment, not verified fact.

Critical press: TechCrunch calls the Rippling/Deel affair 'arguably the biggest drama between two HR startups ever,' and a June 2025 court document showed the confessed spy said he believed men from Deel were following him and his wife was afraid.

TechStartups retracted its Jan 9, 2025 article on the Ponzi-scheme lawsuit after Deel disputed inaccuracies, noting the complaint itself contains no such 'Ponzi' or laundering allegations — example of contested early coverage of the RICO/AML suit.

Current (2026) customer and worker counts from the company — latest company-confirmed figures are 35,000-40,000+ customers and 6,500-7,500 employees (2025).

Company statement (to Calcalist, Sept 2023): ARR of $295 million, up from $57 million a year earlier.
Company claim (Deel blog, filed in litigation context): 35,000+ customers in 150+ countries, $800M run rate, $12bn+ valuation, and profitable for 2.5 years.

Revenue estimate basis (company statements reported by Reuters, June 2025): crossed $1B annual revenue run rate in Q1 2025; revenue +75% for the 12 months ended April 30; EBITDA margin of 16% for Q1 ended March 31, 2025.
Company claim via CEO Alex Bouaziz to Reuters (Oct 2025): revenue crossed $100 million monthly for the first time in September 2025, generating roughly $15-17 million in EBITDA.
Aggregator estimate (ARR.club, labelled aggregator, not company-confirmed): ARR $1.2B (Oct 2025), $1.4B (Mar 2026), $1.5B (Aug 2026); current ARR $1.5B with +19% annualized CAGR.
Company claim (Oct-Nov 2025 reporting): profitable for three years; CEO quoted 'We have been profitable for three years ... revenue crossed $100M for the first time in September.'

Headcount trend (mixed sources): 3,000 team members (March 2024, Calcalist/company) → 5,000 (Feb 2025, Wikipedia) → 6,500 (June 2025, Reuters/company) → 7,500 (2025, Wikipedia); 10 workers at founding per Fortune. No layoffs for Deel were found in pages opened.
Aggregator (AccessIPOs) timeline: 02/04/2025 Deel prepares for IPO as soon as 2026 (citing CNBC); no S-1 filed publicly as of that page's writing.

Company statement (March 2024, Calcalist/CTech): over $500 million ARR achieved organically outside the PaySpace acquisition; 3,000 team members in 100+ countries; EBITDA positive and generating cash for a year and a half.

Headcount trend (mixed sources): 3,000 team members (March 2024, Calcalist/company) → 5,000 (Feb 2025, Wikipedia) → 6,500 (June 2025, Reuters/company) → 7,500 (2025, Wikipedia); 10 workers at founding per Fortune. No layoffs for Deel were found in pages opened.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Rippling filed suit against Deel on March 17, 2025 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleging Deel cultivated a corporate spy to steal trade secrets, sales pipeline and client playbook.

Rippling's amended complaint (June 5, 2025) gets more explicit in accusing Deel CEO Alex Bouaziz of orchestrating the plot, adds a RICO charge, and references defendants as part of a 'criminal syndicate'; it alleges Deel targeted at least four other competitors.

Defendants in Rippling v. Deel Inc. include Deel Inc., CEO Alex Bouaziz, Philippe Bouaziz (CFO/Chairman) and COO Dan Westgarth personally; claims include RICO, Defend Trade Secrets Act and California unfair-competition counts.

Keith O'Brien, a Rippling employee in Dublin, gave a sworn April 1, 2025 affidavit admitting roughly four months of searching Slack and Google Drive on Deel's behalf for a €5,000 monthly retainer paid first in dollars and later in crypto; he was caught after Rippling seeded a fake 'd-defectors' Slack honeypot channel.
Deel countersued on April 24, 2025 in Delaware Superior Court alleging Rippling ran its own espionage scheme; Deel voluntarily dismissed that countersuit in 2026.

Deel's lawyer initially denied following the spy but later discovered Deel did hire surveillance; the Irish Times reported (June 25, 2025) that Deel admitted it instructed 'discreet surveillance' on the manager at the centre of the spy case.

Newly unsealed banking records (reported by Calcalist, Nov 20, 2025) show O'Brien's initial $6,000 payment was routed from a Deel corporate account through an account belonging to the wife of Deel's COO, landing in O'Brien's account 56 seconds later; Rippling is asking what Deel disclosed to its external auditors.

On August 20, 2025 a court dismissed Rippling's RICO and fraud claims (citing the court's finding that Rippling's RICO theory described 'a unified corporate structure, not a distinct RICO enterprise'); remaining trade-secret claims were not dismissed.

A February 2026 federal ruling cleared the Rippling case to move forward, refusing Deel's attempts to dismiss or transfer it; case status as of May 2026: active, RICO claims cleared to proceed, discovery phase.

The Department of Justice reportedly opened a criminal investigation into Deel over the spy allegations (reported by WSJ, Jan 23, 2026); Deel said it is 'not aware of any investigation' and would cooperate with authorities.
DOJ grand jury subpoenas were issued in January 2026 in the Northern District of California as part of the federal criminal probe.

A federal RICO lawsuit filed in January 2025 (Damian v. Deel Inc., S.D. Fla., No. 1:25-cv-20017), brought by a court-appointed receiver from an SEC Ponzi case, accused Deel of flouting AML regulations and facilitating evasion of US sanctions against Russia; Deel denied wrongdoing and moved to dismiss; on August 19, 2025 the S.D. Fla. granted the motion to dismiss and the case was closed.

CFTC investigation reporting (The Information/Calcalist, Sept 2023): Deel facilitated over $72 million in payments between November 1, 2021 and October 14, 2022 (40,000+ transactions) for MyForexFunds, a trading platform the CFTC accused of operating a Ponzi scheme, serving 15,664 of its customers; Deel said this was less than 1% of revenue and it froze the account once informed.

In March 2023 former workers claimed they were mis-categorized by Deel; in June 2023 California state senator Steve Padilla formally asked the California Labor and Workforce Development Agency to investigate the allegations; Deel denied the allegations and engaged with lawmakers.
Regulatory posture: Deel has not been accused of any wrongdoing by the SEC; its DPayments subsidiary held 26 state money-transmission licenses as of early 2025.

Deel said the January 2025 complaint was 'deeply inaccurate and includes wild mischaracterizations of our business' and that it complies with all laws, filing to dismiss; it noted a co-filer was reported to be an early investor in rival Rippling.
